front_blocks.md: Define **HTML**.

back_blocks.md: HTML, or **Hypertext Markup Language**, is the foundational language used to **structure content on the web**.

cards.back_md: HTML, or **Hypertext Markup Language**, is the foundational language used to **structure content on the web**.

front_blocks.md: What are HTML elements often referred to as?

back_blocks.md: HTML elements are often referred to as **tags**, which are used to **structure and format** a webpage.

cards.front_md: What are HTML elements often referred to as?
cards.back_md: HTML elements are often referred to as **tags**, which are used to **structure and format** a webpage.

front_blocks.md: Which tag is the root element of an HTML page?

back_blocks.md: The `<html>` tag is the root element, and it **includes all other HTML elements** used on the page.

cards.front_md: Which tag is the root element of an HTML page?
cards.back_md: The `<html>` tag is the root element, and it **includes all other HTML elements** used on the page.

front_blocks.md: What does the head section of a webpage contain?

back_blocks.md: The head contains **information about the web page that is not displayed on the page itself**. Its content is shown in the **browser tab**.

cards.front_md: What does the head section of a webpage contain?
cards.back_md: The head contains **information about the web page that is not displayed on the page itself**. Its content is shown in the **browser tab**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The content of the head tag is displayed in the browser window.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Content in the **head** is displayed in the **browser tab**, not on the page. It is the **body** content that appears in the browser window.

cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: What does the `<title>` element do?

back_blocks.md: It sets the **page title that displays in the browser tab**, and is placed inside the `<head>` section.

cards.back_md: It sets the **page title that displays in the browser tab**, and is placed inside the `<head>` section.

front_blocks.md: How is an external stylesheet linked to a page?

back_blocks.md: Using the `<link>` element in the `<head>`, with `rel` set to **'stylesheet'** and `href` containing the **relative file path** to the CSS file.

cards.front_md: How is an external stylesheet linked to a page?
cards.back_md: Using the `<link>` element in the `<head>`, with `rel` set to **'stylesheet'** and `href` containing the **relative file path** to the CSS file.

front_blocks.md: Why does the order of linked stylesheets matter?

back_blocks.md: Stylesheets are **loaded in the order they are listed**, so **hierarchy** is important.

cards.front_md: Why does the order of linked stylesheets matter?
cards.back_md: Stylesheets are **loaded in the order they are listed**, so **hierarchy** is important.

front_blocks.md: Define **metatag**.

back_blocks.md: A metatag is a snippet of text in HTML that **describes a page's content**. It appears **in the page's code**, not on the page itself.

cards.back_md: A metatag is a snippet of text in HTML that **describes a page's content**. It appears **in the page's code**, not on the page itself.

front_blocks.md: Name three metatags.

back_blocks.md: Metatags include **charset**, **keywords**, **author**, **description** and **viewport**.

front_blocks.md: What does the description metatag do?

back_blocks.md: It provides a **concise explanation of the content** of the web page. It often appears in **search engine results** and can influence click-through rates.

cards.front_md: What does the description metatag do?
cards.back_md: It provides a **concise explanation of the content** of the web page. It often appears in **search engine results** and can influence click-through rates.

front_blocks.md: What does the viewport metatag control?

back_blocks.md: It controls the **viewport size** and the **initial zoom level**, so the page displays correctly on **all devices**.

cards.front_md: What does the viewport metatag control?
cards.back_md: It controls the **viewport size** and the **initial zoom level**, so the page displays correctly on **all devices**.

front_blocks.md: What does the body section of a webpage contain?

back_blocks.md: The body contains the **main content of the web page**, such as **text, images, videos, hyperlinks and tables**, which is displayed in the **browser window**.

cards.front_md: What does the body section of a webpage contain?
cards.back_md: The body contains the **main content of the web page**, such as **text, images, videos, hyperlinks and tables**, which is displayed in the **browser window**.

front_blocks.md: What are tables mainly used for in webpages today?

back_blocks.md: Tables are primarily used for **displaying tabular data**, meaning information that is logically displayed in a **grid format**.

cards.front_md: What are tables mainly used for in webpages today?
cards.back_md: Tables are primarily used for **displaying tabular data**, meaning information that is logically displayed in a **grid format**.

front_blocks.md: How do tables enhance accessibility?

back_blocks.md: **Screen readers** for visually impaired users can read tables effectively if they are **correctly structured** using elements such as `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>` and `<td>`.

cards.back_md: **Screen readers** for visually impaired users can read tables effectively if they are **correctly structured** using elements such as `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>` and `<td>`.

front_blocks.md: How do you link to a bookmark on the same page?

back_blocks.md: Use the `<a>` tag with an `href` value set to **# followed by the id** of the bookmark, for example `<a href="#section1">`.

cards.front_md: How do you link to a bookmark on the same page?
cards.back_md: Use the `<a>` tag with an `href` value set to **# followed by the id** of the bookmark, for example `<a href="#section1">`.

front_blocks.md: What does the target attribute `_blank` do?

back_blocks.md: It opens the link in a **new tab or window**, whereas `_self` opens it in the **same tab or window**.

cards.front_md: What does the target attribute `_blank` do?
cards.back_md: It opens the link in a **new tab or window**, whereas `_self` opens it in the **same tab or window**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a relative and an absolute file path?

back_blocks.md: A **relative** path gives the location **in relation to the file that references it**. An **absolute** path gives the **exact location regardless of the current location**, including the entire path from the root directory.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a relative and an absolute file path?
cards.back_md: A **relative** path gives the location **in relation to the file that references it**. An **absolute** path gives the **exact location regardless of the current location**, including the entire path from the root directory.
